title: Todd and the Audience of One Chair
synopsis: Todd practices reading his bup page to a chair, while Kim chooses how she would like to participate without public speaking.
continuity_state: Before: Ben has agreed to lend the intact blue book and has it in its cloth bag at his home. The sharing table is on Sunday and the library drop-off trip is Saturday. After: The friends agree on an optional, flexible way to share the book: Ben holds it, Todd may bup, Wendy may show wind, Sue may joke, Kim may point or simply listen, and Amy may open her real yellow map. No one must perform. The Story House chair and props stay put; Ben takes the book home after rehearsal. Todd, Kim, Wendy and Sue retain their established things.

related_resources.reason: The audience-of-a-chair scene is pretend play; AAP play literature supports a general editorial interest in play but not outcomes from these stories.
NAEYC discusses respectful community participation in educational settings, not a single mandated way to share an invented book.
